descriptions.Always: The rule applies at all times. No event starts the check.
descriptions.Agent loop: An event in the agent's own work loop: a prompt arrives, a response goes out, a turn or task ends, a session starts.
descriptions.Agent loop > Prompt received: A user prompt or request reaches the agent.
descriptions.Agent loop > Response sent: The agent makes or sends a response, an answer or a message.
descriptions.Agent loop > Task completion: The agent ends its turn or its task.
descriptions.Agent loop > Session start: A session starts, or the agent loads or compacts its context.
descriptions.Agent action: The agent uses a tool: it writes or reads a file, runs a command, asks the user, or calls a skill, a subagent or an MCP server.
descriptions.Agent action > File write / edit: A file or code is created, changed, renamed or deleted.
descriptions.Agent action > File read: A file is read, opened or loaded.
descriptions.Agent action > Shell command: A shell or CLI command runs, such as a test run, a build or a linter that the agent starts.
descriptions.Agent action > Ask user: The agent asks the user a question (for example with AskUserQuestion).
descriptions.Agent action > Skill / subagent: The agent calls a skill or starts a subagent.
descriptions.Agent action > Tool / MCP call: The agent calls any other tool: an MCP server, a web fetch or search, an external API.
descriptions.Git / delivery: A version-control or delivery event: commit, push, merge, pull request, deploy, release, publish.
descriptions.Git / delivery > Commit: A git commit or a commit message is made.
descriptions.Git / delivery > Push / merge: A push, a merge or a rebase (what starts a CI pipeline on it).
descriptions.Git / delivery > Pull request: A pull request is opened, updated, reviewed or merged (what starts a review or a CI pipeline on it).
descriptions.Git / delivery > Deploy / release: A deploy, a release, a version tag or a database migration.
descriptions.Git / delivery > Publish: A package, a post or other content is published.
descriptions.App runtime: The running application does something: it serves a request, reads or writes data, logs, fails, reacts to the UI, runs on a schedule, sends a message.
descriptions.App runtime > Request / API call: The application gets or makes an HTTP request or an API call.
descriptions.App runtime > Data read / write: The application queries, stores or changes data.
descriptions.App runtime > Log / error: A log record is written, or an error or exception occurs.
descriptions.App runtime > UI event: A page renders, or a user clicks, types or opens something in the UI.
descriptions.App runtime > Schedule / timer: A schedule or a timer fires, or a calendar date arrives.
descriptions.App runtime > Message send: The application sends a message, an email or a notification.
descriptions.Other: None of the options above fits.
